Cut the Dendrograms of plot_dot_dendro_multi() into Clusters

Source: R/Dendro_clustering.R
cluster_dot_dendro.Rd

Rebuilds the exact hierarchical clustering behind the dendrograms drawn by plot_dot_dendro_multi() and cuts it into clusters of groups (rows), genes (columns), or both. Because natural clusters often sit at different heights of a dendrogram, the default methods cut each branch at its own height instead of using a single horizontal cut, so both the number of clusters and the cut heights are derived from the tree:

  • "inconsistency" (default): a branch is kept as one cluster while none of its merges is unusually high compared with the merges directly below it (inconsistency coefficient, depth 2). Each branch is therefore cut relative to its own spread, which suits clusters at clearly different heights.

  • "dynamic": the hybrid dynamic tree cut of dynamicTreeCut (Langfelder et al., 2008), which uses both the tree shape and the distance matrix. It works best when clusters have broadly similar heights.

  • "fixed": an ordinary horizontal cut at k clusters or height h.

Usage

cluster_dot_dendro(
  dot_df,
  what = c("rows", "genes", "both"),
  method = c("inconsistency", "dynamic", "fixed"),
  deepSplit = "auto",
  cutoff = "auto",
  minClusterSize = 2,
  assign_all = FALSE,
  k = NULL,
  h = NULL,
  seurat_obj = NULL,
  meta_col = NULL,
  new_col = "dendro_cluster",
  output_dir = NULL
)

Arguments

dot_df

The data frame returned by plot_dot_dendro_multi().

what

Character. Cut the tree of the groups ("rows", default), of the genes ("genes"), or both ("both").

method

Character. The cutting method: "inconsistency" (default), "dynamic" or "fixed". See Description.

deepSplit

Integer from 0 to 4, or "auto" (default). Dynamic method only: how readily branches are split into sub-clusters (higher gives more, smaller clusters). "auto" picks the value with the best average silhouette width.

cutoff

Numeric or "auto" (default). Inconsistency method only: branches whose merges all have an inconsistency coefficient at or below cutoff form one cluster. "auto" picks the value with the best average silhouette width.

minClusterSize

Integer. The smallest number of leaves that can form a cluster with the dynamic and inconsistency methods; smaller groups are left unassigned. Default is 2. Not used by the fixed method.

assign_all

Logical. If FALSE (default), leaves that do not clearly belong to any cluster stay unassigned (NA). If TRUE, each of them is assigned to the cluster with the smallest average distance.

k, h

Numeric. Fixed method only: the number of clusters (k) or the height at which to cut (h). Give exactly one.

seurat_obj

Optional Seurat object. If given (together with meta_col), the row clusters are written back to the cells as a new metadata column.

meta_col

Character. The metadata column (one of the meta_cols used in plot_dot_dendro_multi()) whose groups are mapped to cells. Each cell receives the cluster of its group's row; cells of unassigned groups get NA.

new_col

Character. The name of the new metadata column. Default is "dendro_cluster".

output_dir

Character. Optional directory in which the cluster table (CSV) and the coloured dendrogram(s) (JPEG) are saved. Default is NULL (nothing is saved).

Value

A list with:

  • clusters: a data frame with one row per leaf: type ("rows" or "genes"), label, id and var (rows only), cluster (factor, NA = unassigned), dendro_order (position in the dendrogram), cluster_height (height of the merge joining the cluster's leaves) and cut_height (the height at which the cluster's branch was cut: midway between cluster_height and the merge joining it to the rest of the tree).

  • k: a named integer vector with the number of clusters found per tree.

  • selection: a named list with, per tree, the candidate settings and their scores (for "auto" settings), or NULL.

  • plot: a named list of ggplot dendrograms coloured by cluster, with a dashed mark at each cluster's cut height; unassigned leaves are grey.

  • hclust: a named list of the hclust trees that were cut.

  • parameters: the method and the settings that were used.

  • seurat_obj: the updated Seurat object (only when seurat_obj was given).

Details

The trees are taken from the "row_hclust" and "col_hclust" attributes that plot_dot_dendro_multi() attaches to its output. For older results without these attributes, the same trees are rebuilt from the avg.exp.scaled values (Euclidean distance, complete linkage).

With deepSplit = "auto" (dynamic method) or cutoff = "auto" (inconsistency method), every candidate setting is tried and the one with the highest average silhouette width is chosen. Unassigned leaves count as a silhouette of 0, so leaving many leaves out is not rewarded. All candidates are reported in selection.

Note that DotPlot() z-scores expression separately within each metadata column, so when several columns are combined, groups are compared by expression pattern rather than on one absolute scale. This is the same basis as the plotted dendrograms.

References

Langfelder P, Zhang B, Horvath S (2008). Defining clusters from a hierarchical cluster tree: the Dynamic Tree Cut package for R. Bioinformatics 24(5):719-720.

See also

plot_dot_dendro_multi()

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
dot_df <- plot_dot_dendro_multi(seurat_obj, meta_cols = c("cell_type", "seurat_clusters"),
                                feature_df = marker_df, prefix = "PBMC")

# Cut the group dendrogram at variable heights
res <- cluster_dot_dendro(dot_df)
res$clusters
res$plot$rows

# Genes and groups with the dynamic tree cut, and write the group clusters to the cells
res <- cluster_dot_dendro(dot_df, what = "both", method = "dynamic",
                          seurat_obj = seurat_obj, meta_col = "seurat_clusters")
table(res$seurat_obj$dendro_cluster)
} # }
